lessons: LATCH DEMONSTRATED LIVE: SFHG printed +11.4% at 06:47, faded to +8.4% by 07:02 and vanished from the scan. It remained a ranked candidate because the +10% cross had already printed. A snapshot-only scanner would have silently shrunk the universe here.

SPREAD AND HALAL ARE ANTI-CORRELATED TODAY: the three tightest books on the board (IREN 0.04%, ABTC 0.26%, MH 0.39%) were all halal-ineligible, while the halal-eligible pick (AZ) sat at 0.54-0.92%. Big liquid names carry the leverage that fails the ratio test; the names that pass tend to be small and wide. This is a structural tension between the halal gate and the spread veto, not bad luck.

HALAL IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT THE STRATEGY. 103 names crossed +10%; 33 were live-screened; 31 FAILED. Only ANGX, AZ (and the untouched EUDA/HLIT/DAAQ/IPCX) passed. Five names that reached genuine candidacy -- AIRO, NAMI, BIRK, AVAH, JACK -- were rejected on screening, and BIRK/AVAH/IREN were exactly the liquid, tight-book names the strategy most wants.

THE HALAL GATE AND THE SPREAD VETO PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The tightest books of the day (IREN 0.04%, SMCI 0.02%, ABTC 0.26%, MH 0.39%) were all halal-ineligible; the eligible names were small and wide (AZ 0.41-0.92%). Big liquid names carry the leverage that fails the ratio test. This is structural and is the main reason C37 struggles to deploy capital live.

VETO RATE 50% (3/6) IS ON TARGET for the first time -- the modelled optimum is 50-65% and Day 7 ran 90-100%. Post-open alone was 40%, slightly BELOW the band, suggesting the 0.5% cap is now roughly right post-open and remains too tight premarket (1/1 blocked).

THE FILL-ARMING RULE EARNED ITS KEEP. The 10:38 ANGX block was NOT a spread veto -- spread was 0.24%. Price had run 0.85% past the trigger, so a stop would have been a market order. Waiting cost nothing: the ratchet re-armed 6 minutes later at a higher, legitimate level and filled.

EXIT DEPTH MODELLING MATTERS MORE THAN ENTRY DEPTH. Selling 3,040 shares into a 113-share inside bid swept the ladder to 4.24. Booking the naive inside-bid fill would have turned -$29.83 into +$45.60 -- a $75 self-flattery on a single $13k ticket. On seven tickets a day that error compounds into a fictional edge.

ONE POSITION + A SLOW NAME = ONE TICKET. ANGX was held 3h40m and moved in a 2.5% band all afternoon. The one-position rule meant tickets 2-7 ($87,034 of the $100,000 budget) never deployed. C37's $1,541/day assumes rotation through multiple tickets; a day with one quiet holder cannot reach it by construction.
